heroHeadline: FDA Approves mFLUSIVA, the First-Ever mRNA Seasonal Flu Vaccine, Capping a Dramatic Regulatory Turnaround
heroSubtitle: On August 5, the FDA approved Moderna's mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) for adults 50+ — the first mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine ever licensed in the US, with full approval for ages 50-64 and accelerated approval for ages 65+, following a unanimous 9-0 VRBPAC vote on June 18 that reversed a February 2026 refusal-to-file. The approval came days after BioNTech named Guido Oelkers, ex-CEO of Sobi, to succeed co-founder Ugur Sahin as CEO by February 2027 (Aug 3), with Sahin departing to launch a new mRNA startup; BioNTech's Aug 4 Q2 results showed revenue down 59% on weak COVID demand but continued oncology pipeline progress (pumitamig 47.6% ORR in PD-L1-negative NSCLC). Separately, Moderna disclosed on July 31 that its mRNA-1403 norovirus vaccine missed a Phase 3 interim efficacy bar, extending the NOVA 301 trial into a third season.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, WHO, NIH, peer-reviewed publications (NEJM, Nature Biotechnology), BioNTech and Moderna investor reports, and ASCO/AACR 2026 presentations. Timeline covers 2020-12-11 to present.
